result.description:
Zitto Golden Grove Pty Ltd is seeking a qualified and experienced Chef to join our kitchen team at our Golden Grove venue in Adelaide, South Australia.

This position is responsible for overseeing day-to-day commercial kitchen operations within a high-volume café and food service environment, planning and preparing menu items, maintaining food quality standards, coordinating kitchen workflow, assisting with menu development, supervising junior kitchen staff, and ensuring compliance with food safety and operational procedures.

The position requires the exercise of independent judgement, advanced cooking techniques, kitchen coordination and operational decision-making to support the efficient operation of the commercial kitchen. The successful applicant will work primarily within the commercial kitchen and will not perform the duties of a café all-rounder, barista, counter-service attendant or kitchenhand.

The Chef plays a key role in maintaining the quality and consistency of food preparation, supervising junior kitchen staff, coordinating commercial kitchen operations during service periods, contributing to menu development, monitoring stock and food costs, and ensuring the efficient operation of the kitchen. The role requires sound technical cooking skills, strong organisational abilities, and the capacity to exercise independent judgement while maintaining high standards of food quality, operational efficiency, and customer satisfaction.


Key duties and responsibilities include:
•	Plan, organise, prepare and cook meals in accordance with the venue’s menu, recipes and service standards.
•	Prepare and cook a diverse range of menu items using commercial kitchen techniques, equipment and standardised recipes while maintaining consistency, quality and presentation standards.
•	Assist with menu planning, daily specials, recipe development, food costing and portion control.
•	Estimate food and ingredient requirements based on menu demand, service levels and stock availability.
•	Order, receive, inspect, store and rotate food supplies to maintain freshness, quality and food safety compliance.
•	Ensure consistency in food preparation, recipe execution and presentation standards across all menu items.
•	Ensure meals are presented consistently and in accordance with the venue’s quality standards.
•	Coordinate kitchen workflow during busy service periods to ensure meals are prepared and served in a timely and efficient manner.
•	Discuss food preparation, menu items, service requirements and kitchen operations with management, kitchen staff and front-of-house staff.
•	Demonstrate cooking techniques and guide junior kitchen staff in food preparation, cooking, plating and presentation procedures.
•	Maintain and enforce hygiene, food safety, cleaning and workplace health and safety standards within the kitchen.
•	Supervise, train and mentor junior kitchen staff, allocate daily kitchen tasks, and monitor work performance to ensure food quality, consistency and operational efficiency.
•	Monitor kitchen equipment, workstations and storage areas to ensure safe and efficient kitchen operations.
•	Minimise food wastage through accurate preparation, stock rotation, portion control and efficient kitchen practices.
•	Monitor food production costs, stock usage and kitchen productivity, and recommend improvements to maximise operational efficiency while maintaining food quality standards.
•	Assist management with production planning, kitchen rostering and workflow scheduling to support efficient daily operations.
•	Operate and monitor commercial kitchen equipment including grills, ovens, refrigeration systems and food preparation equipment while ensuring safe operating procedures are maintained.


Skills and experience required:
•	Certificate IV in Kitchen Management or an equivalent qualification in Commercial Cookery, Hospitality or a closely related field.
•	At least two years of relevant post-qualification experience as a Chef in a commercial kitchen.
•	Strong knowledge of food preparation, cooking techniques, stock control and kitchen operations.
•	Sound understanding of food safety, hygiene and workplace health and safety requirements.
•	Ability to work under pressure in a busy commercial kitchen environment.
•	Strong organisational, communication and teamwork skills.
•	Ability to train, guide and supervise junior kitchen staff.


Employment Conditions
•	Full-time, ongoing position. 
•	Availability to work a rotating roster, including weekends and public holidays.

Salary: AUD $80,000 – $85,000 per annum plus superannuation

How to apply:
Please submit your resume and cover letter outlining your relevant qualifications, commercial kitchen experience and suitability for the role.
result.title: Chef

As our project workload and client base continue to grow, we are seeking a dedicated Contract Administrator to manage the contractual and administrative side of our testing services. and other stakeholders to ensure project goals are met  Advising senior management on matters requiring attention and assisting in implementing decisions  Overseeing work undertaken by contractors and With a strong focus on accuracy, reliability, and integrity, SBDC has built a reputation for delivering high-quality testing solutions that support the successful delivery of major infrastructure and construction projects.    Our team works closely with builders, concrete suppliers, and engineers to ensure every aspect of testing is carried out in strict accordance with Australian Standards, providing confidence that all materials meet required specifications.    At SBDC Testing, we pride ourselves on being responsive, professional, and solutions focused. Job Title: 	Community Worker 
Salary Range: 	$79,500 - $85,000 | depending on skills level and work experience + superannuation.  
Job Closes Date: 	30 Days   
 
About the Role 
Our client delivers person-centered support that helps individuals live independently at home and stay connected to their community. As their Community Worker, you will empower clients – including seniors, people with disabilities, and those with complex needs – to achieve their goals and participate fully in community life. 
 
Key Responsibility and Duties 
Client assessment and planning 
• Conduct holistic assessments of each client’s physical, emotional, and social needs, identifying strengths and barriers to independence. 
• Develop, implement, and regularly review individualized support, training, and educational programs that align with client goals and NDIS/aged-care plans. 
 
Client support and progress monitoring 
• Interview the clients to understand the nature and extent of their difficulties, then provide direct support or skill-building to resolve social, emotional, and financial challenges. 
• Monitor client progress through regular check-ins and documented observations, reporting outcomes to the care team, family, and funding bodies. 
 
Community engagement and referrals 
• Assess local community needs and available resources for health, housing, employment, training, and social activities, then connect clients to relevant services. 
• Liaise with community groups, welfare agencies, government bodies, and businesses to promote awareness of support services and advocate for client access. 
 
Program development and administration 
• Prepare detailed submissions for funding, resources, and program extensions, along with progress reports for government and referring agencies. 
• Supervise and support clients on probation, parole, or in adult service units, group housing, or government institutions – ensuring compliance and rehabilitation goals. 
 
Requirements 
• 1 year of full-time work experience within community services, social work, or in related positions. 
• Relevant qualifications are required. 
• Strong assessment, communication, and advocacy skills. 
• Ability to work with vulnerable populations and maintain professional boundaries. 
• Current driver’s license and willingness to travel across Brisbane. 
 
Apply now  
• This role directly contributes to meaningful, lasting changes in people’s lives.

Jigalong Community Incorporated is seeking a capable, organised and culturally respectful Office and Town Services Manager to support the Chief Executive Officer and coordinate the day-to-day delivery of office and municipal services in Jigalong Community.

This is a full-time, fixed-term position to 30 June 2027, with any extension subject to continued funding, organisational requirements and satisfactory performance.

Salary: $72,527 per annum plus statutory superannuation and applicable district allowance.

Subsidised partly furnished accommodation is available in Jigalong. Salary packaging may also be available under JCI policy.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The position combines senior office administration, community and stakeholder liaison, governance support, visitor accommodation coordination and administration of the Remote Essential and Municipal Services program with practical oversight of municipal employees and work programs.

The successful applicant must be comfortable undertaking both office-based duties and regular field inspections, establishing priorities, maintaining accurate records, following up work and supporting local employees to deliver reliable community services.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Manage the daily operation of the JCI community office and maintain effective administrative systems, records, correspondence and work schedules.

• Act as a principal contact for community members, the JCI Board, government agencies, contractors and other stakeholders.

• Support Board and community meetings, including agendas, minutes, correspondence and follow-up of actions.

• Coordinate purchasing, quotations, supplies, invoice checking, office resources, telecommunications and other administrative services.

• Administer and support REMS funding, records, reporting, inspections, field surveys and required corrective actions.

• Prepare and coordinate municipal work programs and supervise employees undertaking rubbish collection, landfill maintenance, roads and drainage, public area maintenance, vegetation control, firebreaks, airstrip maintenance and related activities.

• Maintain plant, machinery, vehicle, servicing, asset and work-completion records, including photographs and supporting evidence where required.

• Report essential-services faults and liaise with the REMS Contract Manager, regional service providers, local government and relevant agencies.

• Coordinate visitor accommodation bookings, occupancy records, cleaning arrangements and related administration.

• Train and support local employees in office practices, record keeping, safe work practices and municipal-service requirements.

ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS

• Demonstrated experience in office administration, operations coordination, community services or a comparable role.

• Strong organisational skills and the ability to plan work, supervise employees and follow tasks through to completion.

• Sound computer skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, email and electronic record keeping.

• Effective written and verbal communication skills.

• High personal integrity, sound judgement and the ability to maintain confidentiality.

• A respectful and culturally appropriate approach to living and working in a remote Aboriginal community.

• Current Australian C Class driver’s licence.

• Legal right to work in Australia.

• Capacity to obtain and maintain a satisfactory National Police Certificate and Working with Children Check.

Experience with REMS, municipal services, remote community administration, government-funded programs, staff supervision, governance support, accommodation management, asset records or local government liaison will be highly regarded.

HOW TO APPLY

Applicants must submit:
• a current résumé;
• a covering letter;
• a brief written response addressing the essential selection criteria; and
• contact details for at least two professional referees.

Applications must be submitted through Workforce Australia.

Enquiries may be directed to:

Orlando De Biasi
Chief Executive Officer
Jigalong Community Incorporated
PMB 7
Newman WA 6753

Mobile: 0427 219 132
Email:jigalongcouncil@gmail.com

Applications close at 4:00 pm AWST on Friday 7 August 2026.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people are strongly encouraged to apply.

Location: Hermannsburg, NT 0872
Salary: $80k plus 12% Superannuation
Position: Full time, Permanent

Tjuwanpa Outstation Resource Centre (Aboriginal Corporation), plays a significant role in supporting the Western Arrarnta people residing across 37 outstations near Ntaria (Hermannsburg) in the Northern Territory. Situated approximately 130 kilometres west of Alice Springs, the organisation services over 4,500 square kilometres of Aboriginal Land Trust land.

Since its establishment in 1984, Tjuwanpa has been responsible for administering government-funded programs relating to housing, water infrastructure, electricity, and employment services. The organisation has built a strong reputation for effective governance, sound operational management, and meaningful community engagement. As a leading provider of Indigenous employment and support services in the region, Tjuwanpa is seeking a committed and community-focused Community Worker to join its team.

In this role, you will support employment initiatives and broader community development programs for the Western Arrarnta people. The position requires a culturally aware and proactive individual who can work effectively within remote community settings. You will contribute to improving individual and community outcomes by facilitating access to employment pathways, social services, and essential support systems.

Key Responsibilities:

-	Deliver culturally appropriate support services to community members, particularly in relation to employment and personal development
-	Encourage participation in employment programs, training opportunities, and community initiatives
-	Conduct individual assessments to identify employment barriers and develop tailored employment plans
-	Assist job seekers with resumes, applications, interview preparation, and job readiness skills
-	Establish and maintain strong relationships with local employers to support job placement opportunities
-	Provide ongoing support to individuals who have secured employment to promote job retention
-	Plan and deliver workshops and training sessions aligned with community needs
-	Work collaboratively with outstation residents to address barriers to employment and implement practical solutions
-	Maintain accurate records of services delivered, community engagement activities, and outcomes achieved
-	Provide support in crisis situations and refer individuals to appropriate services where required
-	Advocate for community members to ensure their needs are effectively represented
-	Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of community engagement strategies

Qualifications and Experience:

-	AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma with at least one year relevant experience
-	At least three years of relevant experience may substitute for the formal qualifications
-	Demonstrated experience in community services, preferably within Indigenous communities
-	Strong understanding of the cultural, social, and economic challenges in remote Aboriginal communities
-	Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build trust and rapport
-	Experience in employment services, social services, or similar sectors (highly desirable)
-	Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a remote and challenging environment

If you are passionate about contributing to the well-being and development of Indigenous communities and have the necessary skills and experience, we encourage you to apply.  

To apply for this position, email your resume to recruitment@targetbusiness.com,au.  

Please note only short listed candidates will be contacted and your application will be treated as strictly confidential.
